Multimodal QuantTree stream detector

Source: R/dfr_mmqt.R
dfr_mmqt.Rd

Monitors a stream with a Multimodal QuantTree (mmqt()): the observations are grouped in consecutive batches of nu rows, the first n_train_batches batches train the model, and every later batch is tested. Since it monitors the distribution of the observed features, it is primarily used for virtual concept drift.

Usage

dfr_mmqt(target_feat = NULL, nu = 128, n_train_batches = 64, model = NULL, ...)

Arguments

target_feat

Names of the columns to be monitored. NULL (the default) monitors every numeric column.

nu

Number of observations per batch.

n_train_batches

Number of batches used for training. Ignored when model is given.

model

A trained mmqt() model. When given, every batch is tested and reset_state() keeps the model.

...

Further arguments for mmqt() (bins, alpha, n_modalities, alpha_modalities, max_modalities, calibration, n_repeats, n_sim, seed).

Value

dfr_mmqt object. After fit(), drifter_output holds, on the last observation of every tested batch, the assigned modality, the statistic and the threshold, and obj$model the trained model.

Details

Each batch is tested on its own (MMQT is a one-shot test, with a false positive rate alpha per batch), so the detector reports a drift on the last observation of every batch whose statistic exceeds the threshold of its modality. reset_state() forgets the model it trained and trains a new one on the next n_train_batches batches. Rows with missing values are skipped.

References

Stucchi, D., Magri, L., Carrera, D. and Boracchi, G. (2023). Multimodal batch-wise change detection. IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems, 34(10), 6783-6797. doi:10.1109/TNNLS.2023.3294846

Boracchi, G., Carrera, D., Cervellera, C. and Maccio, D. (2018). QuantTree: histograms for change detection in multivariate data streams. Proceedings of the 35th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 80, 639-648.

Examples

library(daltoolbox)
library(heimdall)
# Batches alternate between two modes; from batch 50 the first mode moves.
set.seed(1)
batch <- function(center) data.frame(x = stats::rnorm(64, center), y = stats::rnorm(64, center))
centers <- c(rep(c(0, 4), 25), rep(c(1.5, 4), 10))
stream <- do.call(rbind, lapply(centers, batch))
detector <- dfr_mmqt(nu = 64, n_train_batches = 40, bins = 8, n_repeats = 2, n_sim = 2000, seed = 1)
model <- fit(detector, stream)
model$model$n_modalities
#> [1] 2
which(model$drifter_output$statistic > model$drifter_output$threshold) %/% 64
#>  [1] 51 53 55 57 59 61 63 65 67 69
